I give up. I can't produce a compiling proof of this statement in a reasonable effort, and I didn't modify the file.

The `_solution` is `False`, so the goal is to exhibit a continuous `f` that is not identically zero but has zero integral over every radius-1 sphere. I checked that `f(x) = sin(π‖x‖)/‖x‖` (with value π at the origin) works. For a sphere of radius 1 centred at distance r from the origin, the spherical mean is proportional to (1/r)·[F(r+1) − F(|r−1|)] with F(t) = cos(πt) − 1, and both terms agree for every r > 0. So the statement is true, and the iff holds.

The obstacle is Lean. Verifying the sphere integral needs the surface-measure change of variables for `μH[2]` on `sphere C 1` in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`. Mathlib has `HaarToSphere` (Haar measure to sphere measure) and general Hausdorff measure, but I found no lemma connecting `μH[2]` on a sphere to a radial or polar formula. Building that bridge from scratch is a large formalization project, which is beyond what I can finish here.
